title: devkit.json
description: A project's config: how it uses the kit, and the facts about itself the kit needs. It sits at the project root and is project-owned. The code reviewer reads it from the project's checkout on every run, the generator turns it into the project's kit-owned files, and the apps machine reads from it how to deploy the project. All validate against this file through one small interpreter (plugin/devkit-config.mjs), which understands only the keywords used here: a new keyword fails its tests until it learns it.

$schema.description: Where this schema lives, for editors. Ignored by the kit.

modules.description: The kit's modules the project uses. Only "process" exists so far, so it must be listed; "web" and "canvas" are accepted and not yet acted on.

kit.description: The kit commit the project's kit-owned files were last generated from, as a full or abbreviated SHA. For the record only: whether a project is behind the kit is decided by regenerating its files, not by this value.

reviewer.description: How the code reviewer sets the project up and tests it. Commands run with `sh -c` from the project root of a fresh checkout, without the code reviewer's own credentials in their environment.

setup.description: Run once after each checkout, before the tests and before any agent works in the tree, to install dependencies and the like. Must be safe to run again on a tree it has already run in.

tests.description: The project's test suites. Each is run on every audit round, and its result is put in front of the auditors; the fixer is told to run them.

name.description: A short name for the suite, shown in the reports.

command.description: The shell command that runs the suite. A non-zero exit is a failing suite.

env.description: Environment variables for the project's setup, test and nightly check commands, and only for them. This file is committed, so it holds no secret. A name the code reviewer keeps for itself, `DATABASE_URL` say, may be set here; it reaches the project's commands without ever entering the code reviewer's own environment.

databases.description: The environment variables that each need a database of their own. Before setup, the code reviewer creates one empty Postgres database per name on the machine it runs on, of that machine's Postgres version, and puts each one's address in its variable for the project's setup, test and nightly check commands, over a value `env` gives the same name. Each database's name ends in `_test`, for a suite that refuses any other. The databases are dropped after the run. A machine that cannot create them fails the run, saying what is missing.

harnessNotes.description: Path, relative to the project root, to a project-owned doc of notes for the testing auditor: how the suites are laid out and the conventions they follow. It must exist in the checkout; a path that leaves the project is refused.

redundancy.description: How many auditors look at each quality characteristic in a full round. More finds more and costs more. Defaults to 1.

extraContext.description: Free text about the project for the code reviewer.

nightly.description: What the code reviewer does for the project each night besides its sweep.

checks.description: The project's nightly checks: commands too slow to run on every pull request, run once a night instead. They run after the project's sweep, in the order written, in a fresh checkout of the default branch at its head, after `reviewer.setup`, with `reviewer.env` and databases of their own for `reviewer.databases`, and without the code reviewer's own credentials. No agent runs. A check that fails does not stop the checks after it, and opens an issue in the project with the end of its output; the issue is closed when a later night's checks all pass. A project that lists none gets no checkout and no run. No two checks may have the same name: a check's result is reported by its name.

name.description: A short name for the check, shown in the log and in the failure issue.

command.description: The shell command that runs the check, with `sh -c` from the project root. A non-zero exit is a failing check, and so is a check stopped for running longer than a check may: thirty minutes, unless the machine is set otherwise.

deploy.description: How the apps machine deploys the project: what it runs to put the default branch's build in service, and how it tells that the app is up. Read from the commit being deployed. Commands run with `sh -c` from the root of a fresh checkout of that commit, as the app's own user, with the app's settings in their environment. A project that is not deployed leaves the section out, and nothing else about it changes.

setup.description: Run first in the new checkout, to install dependencies and the like.

build.description: Run after setup, to build what start runs. The app that is running is not touched until this has succeeded.

migrate.description: Run after the running app is stopped and before the new build is started, to bring the app's database to what the new build expects. A project that migrates as it starts, or has nothing to migrate, leaves it out.

start.description: Starts the app, and keeps running for as long as the app does. It must listen on `port`, on loopback only.

port.description: The local port the app listens on.

healthPath.description: The path, on `port`, that answers with success once the app is healthy, `/healthz` say. A deploy asks it after starting the new build and puts the previous build back if it does not answer in time. It starts with `/` and has no spaces; it is not a whole address.

reviewer.extraContext: The billing module is generated; review its generator, not its output.
